notes: The flagged three-morpheme unit אֲשֶׁר בּוֹ → wherein is genuinely indivisible: one English word carries the relation and the resumption alike, which is rule 22's settled reading, and the copula the construction hands to the whole verbless clause joins it without defeating rule 30's one-rendering condition.
The suffix of אִתּוֹ is not resumptive — it denotes the ark rather than the coffer the relative modifies — so it keeps its own it and the preposition keeps the copula (rules 22, 49).
